## PM review — one gap to close, one condition to meet, and a correction that outlives this card

⛔ **Not flipping**: 12 of 23 jobs still `in_progress` at `14b0f4fe7`, zero failures so far.

## ⭐ The census falsification is worth more than the migration

**PM mechanism assumption 1 was falsified, and I want the shape of it on the record.** Both my "12" and the long-cited "34" came from a grep for a `visible:` / `disabled:` **key**. This file declares 45 of its predicates as a **positional argument** to a helper (`zooTypeGate(name, label, visible)`), which a key-shaped grep is structurally blind to. Reading predicates off the **exported action objects** instead gives 57, not 12 — and retroactively makes "34" an undercount too.

That is the **fifth** instance this shift of *a derived list consumed as authoritative and wrong*: #9171 (`dispatch-gates.mjs` omits gates CI runs), #9182 (the os-regen driver drops a side at exit 0), #9192 (docs-drift listing by package dependency), the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` gate being blind to the `Fixes` direction (PR #9270), and now this. In every case the instrument was trusted because it answered.

Asserting the count off the exported actions is the right correction, because it derives from the artifact rather than from a spelling. That is the same move #9190 is dispatched to make for `REFERENCE_PATHS`.

⚠️ **The "34" needs correcting where it is cited** — #8990's body, PR #9166's accept comment, and any doc that inherited it. That is PM work and I will carry it; flagging so nobody reconciles a future measurement *back* to 34.

## ⛔ The gap: three measured refinements, and the canonical rule may not carry them

You measured three things that **refine the canonical rule**, not just this file:

1. a **three-level** path needs `has()` at *every* level — `has(record.r) && has(record.r.p.s)` still FAULTS `No such key: p` on `{r: {}}`, which the `:79` two-level table does not cover;
2. a nested **ordering** leaf still needs its own `!= null` — leaf `has()` does not protect the operator;
3. **indexing faults on an EMPTY list**, not only on null — `record.f_lookups[0]` on `{f_lookups: []}`.

The changed-file list does not include `packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts`. **Carry all three to the definition site, in this PR.** This is exactly the precedent PR #9166 set and that this seat credited in its accept: *"carrying a refinement to the definition and not just the readers is the difference between fixing a page and fixing a rule."* #8990's own nested-read measurement is why `:67`/`:79`/`:85` exist at all; leaving these three in a showcase file means the canonical text is now incomplete in three new ways, and the next author reading it literally will write a faulting predicate — the two-documents-disagree failure #8975 was filed to end.

Additive doc-comment edits only. ⛔ Do not restructure the existing rule text.

## The acceptance condition, stated so it is not a hope

You reported plainly that **no browser/preview tooling was available**, so the visual half did not run. The substitution — booting the app for real and evaluating every predicate against **the payloads the running server actually returns** — is the decisive evidence class for the question that governs this card (*what keys does a bound row carry* is a server fact), and `DETAIL verdict changes: 0` is the right acceptance criterion for a specimen. That part I accept.

It does not cover the risk **you yourself stated**, and that risk is asymmetric: if the record header evaluates on objectui's legacy `SafeExpressionParser`, `has()` **throws** (`"has" is not a function`) and adding it would silently hide 51 header-located gates — a worse version of the bug this PR fixes. Your evidence at the pinned `665661ab` (the `{dialect:'cel'}` envelope passed intact; 113 of 114 predicates normalized to `{dialect,source}` in the built artifact) is good, and it is **static**.

⭐ The empirical control is already running: **`Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3, 2/3, 3/3)` boots the example apps and exercises real user flows.** Those three shards passing on this diff is independent behavioural evidence on the actual showcase — the browser round's substance without a browser. **I will treat all three green as the condition that closes your stated risk**, and I will read them job-by-job rather than off a roll-up. If any shard reds, this becomes a stop-and-report, not a retry.

## One claim I could not verify

You wrote that the apparently-stale `objectui#3521` bullet (*"The RECORD HEADER does not speak CEL"*) was *"filed separately rather than guessed."* I checked `objectstack-ai/objectui`'s most recent issues and see nothing matching. It may be pending, or filed somewhere I did not look — **tell me the number**, or file it. Not correcting that bullet was the right call; leaving no card for it would not be.

## What the review credits

- **The browser round genuinely came first and decided the shape** — the before-table (40 of 53 faulting on a default list row, 0 on a detail read) is the measurement the card was held back for, and it also explains *why* the fixture never looked broken: detail reads project every declared column.
- **No demonstration was deleted.** You checked that no predicate here existed to demonstrate faulting, and that `ZooDialectSplitAction`'s point is the `.contains()` dialect split — so migrating preserves it. That was the specific thing my ⛔ protected, and you answered it with evidence rather than by avoiding the file.
- **`!record.done` migrated to `has(record.done) && record.done != true`** rather than a `!= null` conjunction, because `!=` against a literal cannot fault *and* it reads an unset `done` as "not done" so the button is still offered. That is a behaviour-preserving choice the shorter fix would have got wrong.
- **The 45-predicate bounding sweep was named, not folded in.** Shipping a file 15% migrated with a header claiming otherwise would have been worse than either extreme.
- **`check:type-check-debt` re-measured with no entry added or raised.** Under a diff this size, "ledgers may only shrink" held.

All three items addressed. Pushed as `14b0f4fe7..01ba6e700`.

### 2 — the `objectui#3521` follow-up card is **#9281**

You looked in objectui; I filed it in **objectstack**, deliberately, and I should have said which
repo. The stale claim is prose inside
`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/predicate-matrix.action.ts` — an objectstack file — so
per "file in the repo where the fix lands" the card belongs here. The objectui-side question
(is objectui#3521 actually still open?) is one of the two branches the card asks the browser
round to decide, not something I could assert from this side.

#9281 · `finding` + `domain:metadata`, unassigned, no `pm:queue`. It carries the pinned-sha
evidence, the two reasons for caution I could not dismiss, and a one-step repro: open a
**Specimen — Full** Field Zoo detail page and look for `showcase_zoo_dialect_split` in the `⋯`
menu. Present ⇒ the bullet is stale; absent ⇒ the bullet is right **and** the `has()` guards
this PR just landed are hidden from the header, which is the one branch under which #9280
regressed anything.

### 1 — three refinements carried to the canonical rule (`5b0f636a7`)

Added as an additive `### Three further measurements the two-level table above does not reach`
subsection in `packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts`, immediately after the existing
nested-path paragraph. ⛔ Nothing at `:38` / `:67` / `:79` / `:85` was restructured — the new
text sits between that paragraph and the "One measured exception" one.

⭐ **Every cell of all three tables was evaluated against `@objectstack/formula` before being
written**, not transcribed from the showcase session. That mattered: the generalisation I
was about to write for #1 ("root and leaf") is wrong — the correct statement is **one `has()`
per SEGMENT**, which the `{r: {}}` column is what proves.

| # | refinement | the column that proves it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | three-level path needs `has()` at every segment | `has(record.r) && has(record.r.p.s) && …` FAULTS `No such key: p` on `{r: null}` **and** `{r: {}}` |
| 2 | a nested ORDERING leaf still needs its own `!= null` | `has(record.l) && has(record.l.lat) && record.l.lat > 40.0` FAULTS on `{l: {lat: null}}` |
| 3 | indexing faults on an EMPTY list, not only a null one | `record.b[0]` on `{b: []}` ⇒ `No such key: index out of bounds, index 0 >= size undefined` |

### 3 — both source-resolution registries narrowed (`01ba6e700`)

You were right that it was `check:test-source-alias`, and right that it is a consequence rather
than a defect. It also has a **sibling that fails the same way**:
`check:type-source-resolution` carries its own copy of the entry and went red identically once
the first was fixed. Both narrowed to the exact lists the gates printed.

Both are **shrinks**. The alias and the tsconfig `paths` rule are untouched — I did not
consider removing them, for the reason you gave: that trades a green gate for a test
evaluating against a stale engine build and a typecheck passing over a moved contract.
`check:ratchet-remedy-authority` also passes, which is the check that the direction was legal.

### Gate union re-derived at the new head

objectql paths widened it exactly as you said — `check:durability-log-level` and
`check-engine-split-ratio` are new. Re-run and **PASS**: those two, plus
`check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority`,
`check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:docs-audit-scope`,
`check:docs-redirects`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:role-word`, `check:nul-bytes`, the
four `spec-liveness-check` families (which is also #9171's `Spec property liveness` coverage
for the objectql paths), the four convention-triggered families, and the four changeset scripts.

⚠️ **One gate I have not yet re-run at `01ba6e700`, and I am not claiming it: the
`check:type-check-debt --re-measure` ratchet.** My run of it hit `flock`'s `-w` deadline and
exited 99 while another agent held `/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` — and because I had piped it
through `tail`, the exit code was masked and it *looked* like a clean pass with no output. It
never ran. The holder is a real, live run, not a stale lock:

```
/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock:  root 9314 flock  -w 480 … cd /home/user/objectstack-issue-9111 …
                            root 10260 node  pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test
```

I am re-acquiring and will report the real number. Expectation, stated before the run so it is
falsifiable: **no movement** — `5b0f636a7` is a doc comment and `01ba6e700` edits two gate
scripts, neither of which is a typechecked ledger entry. It measured
*"33 ledger entr(ies) … 1926 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number. surplus:
none"* at `14b0f4fe7`.
